description: §8.2 — the shipped draft. `filters` run in order and are all-or-nothing; `weights` multiply in order onto a card's base share. Every number here used to be a literal in draft.ts, which meant asking 'what if the pool leaned differently' was a commit rather than a measurement.

stats.title: Gain
stats.body: +{n} damage on every Action you own.

stats.title: Precision
stats.body: +{n} crit chance. A crit deals double damage and fires On Crit.

stats.title: Reach
stats.body: +{n} range. Projectile flight distance, beam length, chain jump distance.

stats.title: Capacitor Bank
stats.body: -{n} dash cooldown, and +0.05s of dash i-frames.

stats.title: Coolant
stats.body: +{n} Heat vented per second. Base venting is 8.

stats.title: Capacitor
stats.body: +{n} Cycle capacity for each Program row that is not live.

stats.title: Salvage
stats.body: Each Purge also adds +4% output permanently, on top of the +4% a Purge already gives.

stats.title: Momentum
stats.body: +{n} output for each second since you were last hurt, up to +{cap}. Resets to zero when you take damage.

stats.title: Ballistics
stats.body: +{n} Pierce and +20% projectile speed. Projectiles only.

stats.title: Yield
stats.body: +{n} radius on bursts, fields, mines, vortices and shoves.

stats.title: Half-Life
stats.body: +{n} duration on fields, mines, orbitals, vortices and buffs.

description: The experiment behind the trigger famine: offer a Trigger even when every row already has one. Measured on the shipped pool, 40% of draft moments have no free Trigger slot and 47% none free for an Action, so past draft six the offer is modifiers and filler and nothing else. Everything but `filters` is inherited — the point of a variant is that it states its difference and nothing else, or two policies drift apart in the fields nobody meant to change.

No pool intelligence at all: no hunger, no empty-slot pull, no inert penalty, no Axiom lean. The control group. Every reading about what the weighting buys is a comparison against this, and there has never been one to compare against.
